Website design in Longview, TX has to fit a city that gets things done. Longview had 81,638 residents at the 2020 census, and the metro area around it, Gregg, Harrison, Rusk and Upshur counties, counted 286,184. That is a lot of people who need a roofer, a dentist, a mechanic or a caterer, and most of them start with a search on their phone. Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites for the owner-operators who serve them, with every page written by hand and a free demo shown before any price is discussed.

Longview at a glance, for a business owner

  • City population81,638 (2020 census)
  • Metro area286,184 across Gregg, Harrison, Rusk and Upshur counties
  • IndustryChemical manufacturing at Eastman's Longview site, oil field service, and large distribution, including the Gap Inc. center announced in 2021
  • Nearby towns your customers live inKilgore, White Oak, Gladewater, Hallsville, Spring Hill, Henderson and Marshall
  • Free business helpThe UT Tyler-Longview Small Business Development Center and the Longview Chamber of Commerce

A working town with money moving through it

Longview's paychecks come from places that make and move things. Eastman runs a large chemical manufacturing site here. In 2021 Gap Inc. announced a distribution center of roughly 850,000 square feet in Longview, a $140 million project built first to ship Old Navy's online orders. Eastman also planned a molecular recycling plant here; in 2025 the federal government cancelled its $375 million grant for that project, and that August Eastman said it was delaying construction and reassessing the project's scope and timing. Whatever happens with that plant, the pattern is clear: big employers bring in workers, and workers need everything a small business sells.

That is where the opportunity sits for a local shop. New arrivals do not have a barber yet, or a family doctor, or a guy who fixes garage doors. They search for one. The business that comes up with a clear, honest, fast site gets the first call. The one with only a Facebook page usually does not.

Who the Longview sites are for

Mostly people who run the business and do the work at the same time. Electricians and HVAC techs who serve homeowners from Hallsville to Spring Hill. Salons and barbers off Judson Road. Family dental and chiropractic offices. Caterers and barbecue joints that feed shift crews. Attorneys, insurance agents and real estate agents who need to look established before anyone picks up the phone. Small shops downtown that have done fine on word of mouth and now want the people who just moved here to find them too.

If that sounds like you, the right site is not a big one. It is one that says exactly what you do, where you do it, and how to reach you, on a phone, in a few seconds. Starter covers that for most single-location businesses. If you send crews to five or six towns, Pro adds a city page for each of them.

What we usually find on Longview business websites

Most small business sites in Gregg County fall into one of three situations. Each one has a plain fix.

Only a Facebook page

Google has almost nothing to show when someone searches your name, never mind your service. The fix is a real site on a domain you own, with a page for each thing you do.

A site nobody has touched

The phone number on it does not match the one on the truck, and the hours changed two summers ago. The fix is a rebuild, and after that, updates are part of hosting and maintenance.

A rented platform

Stop paying and the site disappears, and sometimes the domain was never in your name. The fix is a one-time build that you own outright, with the domain registered to you.

How web design in Longview, TX turns into phone calls

Longview has fewer competitors than Dallas, which helps, and fewer searches, which means each one matters more. Three things do most of the work, and every one of them is in the build rather than sold as an extra.

  1. A complete map listingFor anything typed with "near me", the map results sit above the regular results. A filled-in Google Business Profile with real photos and reviews does more for a Longview shop than almost anything else. Pro and Agency include setting it up.
  2. A page for each service and each townOne page that says "serving East Texas" does not tell Google much. Separate pages for what you do in Longview, Kilgore, White Oak or Hallsville give it something to match, as long as each one is written for that place.
  3. Speed on a phoneMost people looking you up are standing in a parking lot or a driveway. If the page takes five seconds, they are gone. Every site we build is made to load fast on a phone.

None of this lets anyone promise a ranking or a number of calls, and we will not. It does give your site the foundation search engines look for. You can check what your current site is missing with the free Site Check.

Free help for Longview owners

The UT Tyler-Longview Small Business Development Center gives free advising to businesses in Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Panola, Rusk and Upshur counties, with offices in Longview, Marshall, Jefferson and Henderson. The U.S. Small Business Administration named it the 2024 SBDC of the Year for the North Texas region. If you need a business plan, a loan package or a second opinion on cash flow, it is the first call to make.

The Longview Chamber of Commerce lists business resources and connects members with the SBDC. In a city this size, the referrals that come out of a chamber lunch still matter. We have no arrangement with either one; they are simply worth knowing.

Common questions

What should website design in Longview, TX cost a small business?

Expect anything from a cheap template you rent by the month to a few thousand dollars from an agency. Dominion Web Design Pro charges once: $497 for Starter, $997 for Pro, $1,997 for Agency. After launch, hosting and maintenance are $49 a month, or included if you keep the AI chat or phone agent.

Is there a web designer near Longview who builds the site personally?

Yes. Maurice Johnson works from Big Sandy, a short drive west of Longview in Upshur County, and writes every page himself. There is no Longview office and no sales team between you and the person doing the work.

I already have a website for my Longview business. Can you redo it?

Usually that is the easier job. You already know a site matters; the one you have just is not bringing anything back. We build the replacement, you approve it, and then your domain is pointed to the new site. If the old one sits on a platform you rent, we will tell you exactly what moving off it involves.

Does web design in Longview, TX include getting on Google Maps?

Every package puts Google Maps and your hours on the site and submits your titles, descriptions and sitemap to Google. The Pro and Agency packages also include Google Business Profile setup and schema markup, which is what feeds the map listings people see when they search "near me".

How long before my Longview site is live?

A Starter site goes live in 7 to 14 days. The thing that slows it down is almost never the building; it is waiting on photos, hours and the list of services. Have those ready and it moves quickly.

See your Longview website before you decide anything

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
